newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh meeting calls for harnessing rivers.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh meeting calls for harnessing rivers.

text.p: South Asian countries dependent on water from Himalayan rivers called on Tuesday for greater cooperation in exploiting the resource for the benefit of their largely poverty-stricken populations.
The call came as water experts from Bangladesh, India and Nepal began a meeting in Dhaka on "Harnessing the Eastern Himalayan Rivers and Regional Cooperation".

S.A. Malek, political adviser to Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, said the experts would study opportunities for development and cooperation in the Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna (GBM) region that stretches across parts of Bangladesh, India, Bhutan, Nepal and China.

"(This) initiative focuses on water resources of the GBM region as the entry point, but it has also been exploring possibilities of cooperation in other fields such as trade, various aspects of poverty alleviation and sustainable development," Malek said.

Q.K. Ahmed, chairman of Bangladesh Unnayan Parishad which sponsored the conference, said: "We must rise to the occasion and devote our best efforts to make things happen in terms of economic growth, poverty alleviation and social development."
Bangladesh and India signed a landmark 30-year treaty in December for sharing water from the Ganges, which Dhaka calls the Padma, removing the worst irritant in their relations.
Officials said India had also concluded a water treaty with Nepal that had created new opportunities for regional cooperation.
"Let us not waste time by ruminating over our past failures. Let us build our future together," Malek said.
Pierre Landell-Mills, head of the World Bank mission in Bangladesh, called the GBM region a paradox.

"The region is mired in poverty and human suffering. It is home to over half a billion people whose per capita income is substantially lower than that of Sub-Saharan Africa. Over 50 percent are absolutely poor," he told the conference.

"(But) it is a region...rich in natural resources such as water, land, hydropower potential, gas and coal. There is no reason for the region to remain poor if its abundant resources can be harnessed through cooperative efforts by the regional countries," he said.
